prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: a production atlas of circular illustrated tokens for Creation, an original elemental myth about making a vast living world. The reference is the APPROVED STYLE AND CONTINUITY anchor, not a sheet to copy unchanged. Paint new subjects in exactly that family: luminous opaque gouache, selective fine ink contours, strong simplified silhouettes readable at 64px; deep lapis interiors, jade and turquoise, burnt ochre, muted coral, warm ivory light, very narrow ivory-gold rims. Not glossy coins or flat generic pictograms. Each icon is a complete perfect CIRCLE with opaque painted interior and transparent empty space outside. Center each circle in its own equal grid cell, circle diameter 80 percent of the shorter cell side, generous empty gutters. Absolutely no letters, names, numbers, grid lines, labels, UI, watermark or cast shadows outside circles. No modern laboratory hardware, books, houses or buildings. Only the specified object inside each circle, with a simple dark ground or essential local context. Tiny details must not carry the meaning. Related states should differ in structure, not merely colour. Follow item order exactly, left to right, top to bottom. Exactly 20 circles in 5 columns and 4 rows. Landscape atlas. Exact cell subjects: CELL 1, Magnetic field: The recurring dark planet is enclosed by two large symmetric jade field loops that leave one pole and curve back to the other, with a few solar particles diverted around the outside. Distinguish: Paired loops around poles; gravity paths converge on a mass, aurora is confined to a polar sky and tilt has one straight axis. CELL 2, Stone crust: A broad curved slab of dark solid rock shows a cool cracked upper surface and a thin coral glow beneath its cut edge, suggesting a hardened skin over a hot interior. Distinguish: One intact hardened shell section; Earth is a compact raw chunk, moving plates are distinct slabs at a boundary. CELL 3, Aurora: Tall jade and pale-coral curtains hang above a dark curved polar horizon, their lower edges rippling while a few small stars remain visible overhead. Distinguish: Vertical glowing night curtains over one pole, without full globe loops, a daylight bow or layered atmosphere. CELL 4, Giant impact: An oblique small rocky body strikes the rim of the recurring large planet, sending a white-coral fan of debris into a curved orbit while most of the planet remains intact. Distinguish: Visible collision between unequal bodies and an orbiting debris fan; impact winter shows the later darkened world. CELL 5, Tides: The hooked shore appears in miniature under the pale Moon; two broad nested waterlines show the sea at high and low positions against the same rock. Distinguish: Two water levels visibly associated with a Moon; tidal shore emphasizes exposed habitat and lunar rhythm includes multiple phases. CELL 6, First rain: Large bright raindrops fall from a steaming low cloud onto bare dark cooling rock, where a few small wet splashes gleam among still-warm cracks. Distinguish: Bare recently cooled world with steam and hot cracks; later Rainfall is an ordinary shower over established land. CELL 7, Rain-filled hollows: Three irregular shallow basins in bare dark stone hold separate jade pools beneath the last few raindrops; raised dry rock clearly divides the pools. Distinguish: Distinct water-filled depressions on barren crust, before connected sea or vegetation. CELL 8, Ocean: A broad uninterrupted ultramarine sea curves toward a quiet pale horizon, with one deep jade foreground swell and no visible islands or living shore. Distinguish: Expansive connected sea rather than a droplet, a breaking wave sequence or exposed coastal shelf. CELL 9, Tidal shore: A shallow jade sea recedes from a dark hooked cliff, exposing a broad wet ochre shelf dotted with small tide pools; the cliff's small wave-cut arch sits above the shelf. Distinguish: Exposed shore and tide pools dominate; no rich habitat mosaic, tidal double diagram or close cave entrance. CELL 10, Evaporation: A warm ochre sun illuminates a shallow sea, where thin transparent streams rise from the surface and fade into clear air before forming any cloud. Distinguish: Upward movement off a lit water surface, no droplet cloud; pale streams are a process convention, not visible water vapour. CELL 11, Clouds: Two substantial ivory cumulus clouds stack softly above a flat dark lower edge, with cool jade shadows and a few pale gaps between the lobes. Distinguish: Opaque terrestrial cloud masses without falling rain, cosmic dust or low translucent veil. CELL 12, Rainfall: A broad grey-jade cloud releases a visible curtain of slanting pale drops onto an established ochre hillside and a small stream. Distinguish: Ordinary land shower without glowing crust, forest canopy or snow crystals. CELL 13, Rivers: One strong jade river winds from high dark hills across ochre land, fed by two narrow tributaries that merge into its single channel. Distinguish: Tributaries converge into one main flow; braided channels repeatedly divide and rejoin, delta splits toward the sea. CELL 14, Sediment: A low fan of sorted ochre sand, pale pebbles and dark fine silt lies in shallow water, with visibly separate coarse and fine bands along its edge. Distinguish: Water-laid loose grains rather than airborne dust, root-rich soil or hardened striped rock. CELL 15, Delta: A jade river splits into three outward-reaching channels across a triangular ochre sediment fan at the edge of a dark blue sea. Distinguish: Distributary branches fan into the sea; no single trunk valley or inland loops. CELL 16, Rainbow: One bright but restrained multicolored bow arcs between a sunlit cloud edge and a slanting rain shower, with dark blue space inside the curve. Distinguish: Smooth ordered daylight color arc rather than curtains, field loops or circulating process. CELL 17, Water cycle: A compact island cross-section shows a sunlit sea, a cloud above a mountain and a river returning to the same sea, joined by one pale sweeping loop rising on the sea side and descending over land. Distinguish: The whole connected sea-cloud-land-return arrangement is present, with no words or flowchart boxes. CELL 18, Moving plates: Two thick dark crustal slabs meet in cutaway: one bends downward beneath the other while a coral seam opens at the far side. Broad pale motion strokes follow the slabs. Distinguish: Multiple moving slabs and two boundary actions, not an isolated trench or static hardened crust. CELL 19, Continent: A broad ochre landmass with the world's distinctive hook-shaped cape stretches across a jade sea, its inland ridges low and its coastline continuous. Distinguish: Broad connected land seen obliquely, without globe outline, isolated cone or close tidal shelf. CELL 20, Trench: A deep narrow indigo cleft cuts the blue seafloor beside a raised rocky plate edge, shown in cutaway with one slab curving sharply down beneath the other. Distinguish: Extremely deep submarine groove with descending slab, not an open land valley or smoking chimney. Keep the common circle size and painted finish. Anatomical lineages matter: insects have six legs, birds feathered wings, bats membranous finger-supported wings. A depicted early cell is a symbolic magnified view, not a modern laboratory slide. The world is not Earth's recognizable map. People, if listed, have varied warm earth-brown complexions, simplified features and no modern objects. Never add people, plants or animals to a subject that predates them. Do not draw the subject names.
